correspondence.finding: The actual southwestern beginning follows an unnamed small-lake and stream chain northward into a larger western lake, then turns northeast through further lake widenings to join the channel labelled Ellice River. The labelled river approach from farther southeast is a separate approach, not the selected beginning. The lake shapes, connecting watercourses and west-then-east turn are visible on the Beechey Lake sheet.

On the Duggan Lake sheet the selection follows the upper Ellice corridor east and northeast through two prominent unnamed lake widenings, then bends north. The river labels, western sheet-edge connection, successive lake outlets and broad eastward bend match the selected route; the sheet title does not name those selected lakes.

Across the Overby Lake sheet the selection follows the labelled Ellice northward and northeastward, including its middle bends and the northeastern continuation at the northern branch junction. It does not take the northwestward mapped branch, and Overby Lake lies west of the selected river rather than forming a selected lake passage.

The Brichta Lake sheet depicts the selected lower Ellice continuously through the southwest-to-northeast entrance, intervening bends, lake-like widenings and lower northward course near the eastern sheet edge. Direct Ellice River labels accompany this same corridor.

The Queen Maud Gulf sheet shows the northern continuation of Ellice River entering the western side of Campbell Bay. The modeled endpoint reaches that coastal outlet setting, and the bay opens into Queen Maud Gulf. This supports the terminal geography without fixing an exact modern mouth, shoreline or tidal boundary.

The selected upper mainstem takes the east–west upper Nushagak branch and its subsequent southwestward bends into the south-flowing trunk. The recreation map places the Nushagak River label on this actual eastern branch. Its separately mapped Chichitnok approach extends farther north and is not the selected beginning; that neighboring headwater is not substituted for the model route.

The trunk continues south to the western Nuyakuk junction, then past the Koliganek setting to the eastern Mulchatna junction and onward through the New Stuyahok and Ekwok corridor. The mapped junction order, major bends and community positions match the selected mainstem pieces. The northern King Salmon and Chichitnok approaches and other nearby tributaries are not separately selected members.

The western two-piece chain begins at the eastern Tikchik Lake outlet setting and runs generally east through the mapped Nuyakuk corridor into Nushagak above Koliganek. The regional sheet shows the lake, its outlet connection and the successive downstream bends; the recreation map directly labels Nuyakuk River. The selection does not include the full Wood–Tikchik lake complex or the northern Tikchik River approach.

The long eastern chain begins in the Turquoise Lake setting, exits west, swings northwest through the upper Mulchatna valley and then southwest to the Nushagak confluence. Region 7 depicts the distinctive upper route and its separate southern Twin Lakes approach; the recreation map shows the continuation past the Chilikadrotna junction and directly labels Mulchatna River. The actual selection follows upper Mulchatna rather than turning into the separately mapped Chilikadrotna–Twin Lakes chain. Middle and lower selected pieces continue along Mulchatna to Nushagak.

The last mainstem piece follows lower Nushagak south toward Portage Creek, then west and northwest along its lower-channel course toward Dillingham and the head-of-bay outlet setting. Region 5 depicts this distinctive terminal turn and the adjoining coastal water. The selected endpoint is not asserted to be a surveyed river mouth or tidal boundary, and the line is not extended through the whole of Nushagak Bay or Bristol Bay.

The actual southeastern beginning follows a mapped small-watercourse and lake approach into the elongated northward upper Kogaluc lake chain. The short initial feeder has no separately assigned hydronym, and the model starting point is not treated as an official river source.

The northward selected approach corresponds to the upper corridor labelled Kogaluc and the Tukimuattuq/Tukimuattup Qamaninga lake setting. The map title Lac Vernon is not a name for this entire route, and nearby lakes or rivers are not substituted solely because they are labelled.

In the middle, the actual modeled line makes an east-and-north loop in the Tasiat/Anuc lake network before following its northern-western connection toward the Albrutchaq and Anartalik setting. The detailed source shows the connected lake-and-channel setting and also a separate more direct western Kogaluc course from the Tasiat area. The model route is not flattened into that shorter course or used to adjudicate flow division between connections.

The west-northwest continuation matches the Manguic/lower Kogaluc corridor and its series of lake expansions toward Lac Kogaluc. The lake names identify distinct waterbodies rather than alternate names for the whole modeled river group.

After the lower lake setting, the selected end bends north along the mapped lower Kogaluc connection toward Reef Bay, opening to Hudson Bay. The separate Polemond route farther southwest is not the selected terminal. No full bay crossing, open-sea extension or surveyed present mouth vertex is assigned.

The selected northeastern beginning descends through the southwestern Guanaceví Colorado drainage and turns west across the northern Tepehuanes corridor. The municipal relief maps match the actual south-then-west approach. The first short feeder and an official source point are not assigned.

The selection continues southwest along the Colorado corridor and joins the west-flowing Humaya route in northern Tamazula, then follows its long western bend toward El Portezuelo. The eastern El Valle approach and the separate Tamazula river farther south are not substituted for this selected branch.

The actual selected Humaya course enters the northeastern approach of Presa Adolfo López Mateos, traverses the mapped reservoir corridor and continues south below its dam toward Culiacán. The western Badiraguato arm and the separate Dique Mariquita are not selected upstream or reservoir passages.

The northern Humaya approach reaches the Tamazula junction at Culiacán, where the selection turns west into the receiving Culiacán course toward San Pedro and Navolato. The Tamazula approach and Presa Sanalona lie east of the selected route and are not aliases or selected reservoir passages.

The selected western bend near Navolato and following southward bends match the river labeled Culiacán on the Navolato relief map, including its natural connection into the Pabellones coastal-lagoon setting near the end of the mapped river. Adjacent canals, Río Viejo and Laguna de Batoato are distinct. The endpoint does not imply a complete lagoon crossing or continuation through Boca la Tonina to the open Gulf.

scope_limit: MAIN_RIV groups and model mainstem roles do not establish a uniform name for every included reach, tributary or lake passage. Source observations support only the stated representative identity or hold.
publication_boundary: Own factual observations, attribution and official public URLs only; source originals, images, complete coordinates and private evidence remain omitted.
